title: Professional writing tasks took less time
location: Online experiment on Prolific. Participant countries not established from the reviewed article and supplement.
observed_outcome: In a randomized writing experiment, ChatGPT access reduced average task time by 40% and increased assessed output quality by 18%.
ai_contribution: Generated text in response to participants’ writing prompts.
human_contribution: Participants supplied prompts and chose what to submit. Most users submitted unedited or lightly edited AI output. Blinded professionals assessed the writing.
evidence_supports: 453 college-educated professionals completed occupation-specific tasks. Assignment to ChatGPT occurred between two tasks. Three blinded professionals assessed each output.
limitations: Short tasks emphasized generic writing and did not require precise factual accuracy or organization-specific knowledge. About 10–20% of controls also used ChatGPT. This measures immediate task performance, not productivity across a whole job.
tradeoffs: Real work may require fact-checking, context gathering, and other effort absent from the experimental tasks. Effects on employment and pay were not measured.
replication_hypothesis: The experiment used self-contained assignments, introductory guidance, and quality-linked payments. Results do not establish equivalent gains on fact-intensive or organization-specific work.
beneficiaries: College-educated professionals doing the tested writing tasks, with larger quality gains among initially weaker performers.
stakeholder_detail: The 453-person sample included marketers, grant writers, consultants, data analysts, human resources professionals, and managers. It was not a workforce census.

sources.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
Experimental Evidence on the Productivity Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence, author-hosted manuscript
Supplementary Materials for Experimental Evidence on the Productivity Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence

evidence_basis.evidence_design: Preregistered randomized online experiment with a pre-treatment writing task.
evidence_basis.outcome_documentation: The published abstract reports 40% less time and 18% higher output quality. The author manuscript supplies the design, dates, GPT-3.5 identification, and limits.
evidence_basis.verification_limit: Published abstract, author-hosted manuscript, and supplement reviewed. This is a bounded task experiment. Follow-up surveys measured reported adoption, not sustained workplace productivity.

ai_attribution: The comparison estimates the effect of being assigned access and guidance for ChatGPT. It is not a perfectly separated comparison of all AI users against all nonusers.
editorial_classification_note: Use the final publication’s 453-person sample and 40% and 18% summary estimates. Do not mix them with the earlier 444-person working paper or label the quality measure factual accuracy.

system_details.source_note: The author manuscript identifies GPT-3.5 and the experiment dates. It does not give an exact model snapshot or ChatGPT release identifier.

research_data.design: Randomized access to ChatGPT between two incentivized writing tasks

denominators.notes: The paper cross-randomized incentive schemes. The main unrestricted-time productivity figures cover the linear and convex incentive groups, about 80% of participants. Outcomes have differing available observation counts.

measurements.notes: Writing quality, not a factual-accuracy score.

research_data.duration_follow_up: Immediate writing outcomes. Two-week and two-month follow-ups concern reported use at work, not measured productivity gains.
limitations: Short, self-contained tasks without precise factual-accuracy requirements.
Employment and wage effects were not measured.
research_data.source_notes: Online publication July 13, 2023, print issue July 14. Author manuscript pages 3–7 cover methods, results, and limits. Supplement Section A.1 documents prompts and recruitment.
research_data.evidence_status: Peer-reviewed publication with author-hosted primary materials reviewed. Independent replication is not established.

source_checks.claim: The tasks did not require precise factual accuracy or context-specific knowledge
Sample prompts taught drafting, reprompting, and summarization
source_checks.locator: Section A.1, Survey Structure, printed page 2

documented_conditions: Participants worked on short assignments tailored to their occupations.
Treatment participants received ChatGPT signup instructions and example prompts.
Participants received quality-linked payments and output was graded by blinded professionals.
evidence_details.transfer_limit: The measured gain should not be applied directly to research-heavy, fact-sensitive, or organization-specific writing, or to total job productivity.

related.reason: Both examine language assistance for professional communication and report larger gains among initially weaker performers.
related.caution: The writing study tested short tasks with ChatGPT. Customer support used live workflows and a specialized system. Their percentages measure different outcomes.

evidence_details.application_detail: Drafting professional emails, press releases, reports, and analysis plans
